precepts.why:
“And ye shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain: and be ye with the king as he goeth out and as he cometh in.”

In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought the captains into the house of the Lord, took an oath of them and showed them the king’s son. He set them by watches and companies so the house would not be broken down, and this is the order that crowned it: every man armed around the king, anyone coming within the ranges slain, and the guard with him as he went out and came in.

moments.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?
Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal: a mother giving orders to kill anybody next in line, because her power came through her son. Back then a woman was only empowered based on the man; America is empowering you directly now.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: But Jehosheba took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, and hid him and his nurse in the house of the Lord six years. They had to hide that little boy, cuz this is how wicked women are: to stay in power, they'll destroy the men.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought the rulers over hundreds into the house of the Lord, made a covenant with them, showed them the king's son, and set armed guards around him on every side: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: He brought forth the king's son, and put the crown upon him, and gave him the testimony; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, God save the king. That's where that saying comes from: we literally had to deal with wicked women trying to interfere with the rulership of men, and the priest had to establish a king. It's just like our ministry: we're trying to set up things for the King of kings and Lord of lords.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Athaliah rent her clothes and cried, Treason, Treason. She just killed all the royal seed, and when they anoint the rightful king, she screams treason. When you try to restore order, that's how some women look at you, like it's treason against them; they don't see that they're out of order.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Jehoiada the priest commanded, Have her forth without the ranges, and him that followeth her kill with the sword; let her not be slain in the house of the Lord. And they laid hands on her, and by the way the horses came into the king's house, there was she slain. That was the restoring of order: twice in the history, when wicked women rose up in power to devour, God sent men of the Lord to remove them for not listening to what God got to say.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw her son was dead, she moved to destroy all the royal seed so she could seize the throne.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Jehosheba, sister of Ahaziah, took the infant Joash and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, hiding him in the house of the Most High for six years while Athaliah reigned.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought the captains together, took an oath of them in the house of the Most High, and showed them the king's son.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: He commanded them how to guard the king by watches and companies so that the house would not be broken down.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: The guard was to compass the king round about, every man with his weapon in his hand, and to stay with him as he went out and came in.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: The captains did according to all that Jehoiada commanded, taking their men to the priest.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Jehoiada gave the captains King David's spears and shields that were in the temple, and the guard stood every man with his weapons in hand around the king.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Then he brought forth the king's son, put the crown upon him, gave him the testimony, anointed him, and the people clapped their hands and said, God save the king.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and the people and came into the temple, and saw the king standing by a pillar as the manner was.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: She rent her clothes and cried, Treason, treason, but Jehoiada commanded the captains to have her forth outside the ranges.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: She was not to be slain in the house of the Most High, so they took her out by the way the horses came into the king's house and slew her there.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Jehoiada made a covenant between the Most High, the king, and the people, that they should be the Lord's people.
This same covenant is what happens today: as a person wakes up, repents, keeps the commandments, and comes out of idolatry, they again become the Lord's people.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: All the people went to the house of Baal, broke down its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Joash was brought to the throne, the people rejoiced, the city was quiet, and he was seven years old when he began to reign.
